tips.comment: Hey folks, so I have stopped my betting for this month just to give myself a good chance of winning the bigger prizes and only doing the nap as I'm up about 45+ points but only 3 winning selections. So, need another 2 to make it 5 lol. Let's take the win folks as we have had a solid May 2025 :) Dothan comes here in good form having won LTO at Doncaster in handicap debut last month and has to be the one to beat.

Lord Roxby arrives today after a respectable fifth at Doncaster, where he was beaten just under six lengths in a Class 4 handicap. That run followed a solid fourth at Ripon, and he now benefits from a slight drop in the weights. With a favourable low draw and prior success over 5f, he’s poised to be competitive over this 6f trip.
Take a chance on 3yo irish filly Mae Amor here. She was a good 3rd of lto over 6f at Ripon after a 181 day break. Should be even sharper today and she drops in class. Shouldn't be far away.

East Tyrone is a 3-year-old gelding trained by Kevin Ryan. He is 1/9 wins, having won a nursery as a 2-year-old off a mark of 67 and runs today off a lowly 64, a career-low mark. He is out of a pretty ordinary dam who was related to nine winners, two of which posted career-high RPR of 88-105 over today's 6f. Kevin Ryan is 22/83 wins in 6f handicaps since 2012 at Hamilton, showing a healthy LSP of £41.63. East Tyrone should strip a lot fitter today on his second start after a 168-day break and wind surgery under Shane Gray.
Mr Cool did a good job when winning a C5 last month but did not get on with the step up to C3 at Southwell. I think the drop back to C4 and returning to turf today could see him bounce back. EW 4P.
Was last seen last year in November and has since been gelded and undergone a wind operation. Could be dangerous if ready to rumble, especially at his mark. Course and distance winner.

Total outsider of the race, but a proper punt despite that. Second race under Jim Goldie stable and may improve with the jockey having a good record here. Distance should not be a problem as he won at 6f last year.

STIRRUP CUP is one of those hit-and-miss sorts, but there was enough shown in the debut season to suggest there's some ability there. He'd have needed the run last time out after over six months off. Softening ground shouldn't be a problem, as the only win to date at Carlisle was on soft going. That was followed up by a decent class 2 showing at Ayr from today's mark. Not without chance if back in that sort of mood.
Great strike rate with 2-year-olds. 230,000 guineas can run well for the Fahey team. Can run well on debut and can run well with Doyle in the saddle.

Now, the only one in the field of runners with runs under its belt must count as some kind of advantage. Ran green last time out in a small field but showed some promise, and I am surprised it's being offered at such generous odds.
This race has two Havana Grey progeny, and of the two, I fancy Azizam out of a dam Mimram by Kheleyf. This runner is expected to contest the finish and finish ahead of the favorite.
4yo gelding Oriental Prince is in extraordinary form since last October winning 7 from 13 races. Is up 3lbs for his latest win a Haydock and will make another bold bid here.

Three runs from the 7yo this year, not quite getting home in his races but his fitness should be fine now. Solid form last year, including two wins over this 5f C/D while racing off a 2lb and 7lb higher mark. Good jockey booking today and can be a big player.

Hurt You Never returns to Hamilton, where she secured a win earlier this month over 5f. She followed that with a fifth-place finish at Carlisle nine days ago, suggesting she’s still in competitive form.

Veteran who picked up a 5th career victory at Wetherby last April. Wasn't seen much thereafter which indicates injury issues but returned with a fair effort at Southwell last month. Will need to take a step forward from that but he's a better horse on turf and sits below that last winning mark so would be no surprise to see him run well.
Dropped to a useful mark and one that can be involved from this afternoon. Likes the good to soft going, and with rain about, this could aid this one's chances.

Going to take a chance with the in-form yard of Alice Haynes, who doesn't come up here for nothing, and Pop Star is one of two she has sent. Should be ready now after a few blasts and could upset the market leaders.

This horse looks thrown in to me on handicap debut here and looks the best bet of the day. Any horse that starts life in a class 2 maiden at HQ is highly likely to be better than a 72 rated handicapper. He dwelt in that race and shaped as though this extra furlong would suit, so that was a decent debut overall when he had 80-90 rated horses ahead of him. The owner also tends to have a decent calibre of horse, so again that's another clue that this horse should be too good for these.

The Cupa Slates Handicap is a Class 5 race over 1 mile and 68 yards, exclusively for three-year-olds, carrying £4,187. One contender stands out: A War Eagle, trained by the promising Ed Bethell, a young trainer making a name for himself. His yard has been selective with its runners, yielding 2 wins from 11 in the last 14 days. A War Eagle, a well-bred three-year-old, has shown promise across several outings. He debuted in December on Wolverhampton's all-weather track, running a huge race at 22/1, finishing strongly behind Perfect Life. He then contested a 7-furlong race at Newcastle, where he ran respectably but was caught in a typical Newcastle muddle, finishing a few lengths off the pace. After a 71-day break, he returned for his turf debut at Thirsk, where his connections clearly held him in high regard. He was backed as the 5/2 favourite in a 15-runner field. The race was won convincingly by Montpellier (trained by James Ferguson), but A War Eagle paid the price for early exertions, trying to match strides with the front-running City of Poets, ultimately tiring late on.
No need for Obito to be such a big price here. He has run with credit in all 3 races to date, and I think he looks to be still developing/progressive. Great chance here.

Not been beaten that far in their two 3yo handicap's to date and one of those was @ Class 3 level. Down another 2lb here in this class 5, good jockey up and very good trainer who is tops here numerically last 5 seasons, 17 percent with his 3yo's in same period, making current 18/1 solid Ew value in the race.

CYMBIDIUM won her maiden at over 1 mile on good ground at Thirsk in September last year. She has disappointed in 4 subsequent runs. LTO she ran over 10f but drops back in trip here. David O'Meara's yard is in reasonable form with 8 winners in the last fortnight. She can go well at a price.
Sands of Indi should be racing fit after two runs this season and may run better here with a stiff finish in his favor. Any rain would be beneficial.

Sure And Steadfast had excuses on his first attempt over a mile at Ayr a month ago. He was boxed in towards the end of the race that never gave him a chance. With the stable in great form he may do better now on his second attempt over the distance.

Say What You See could be worth another shot as it won in November off a 62 in C6 and was then placed in C5 off a 68. It returned last month and ran no race at all when stepping up to 1m2f. It should be improving while still on a 68 today back at 1m+ EW 4P.
5yo gelding Arkenstar is on a handy mark 2lbs below his last winning mark from last May. His 5 career wins came all here at Hamilton. Goes well on todays ground and will be in the mix here.

Dow & Low Handicap (Class 5, 1m 68y, 4yo+). Several familiar names line up, many struggling to win - including Swift Salian, trained by David Barron. Once a master tactician, Barron now manages a smaller stable but remains effective. Swift Salian has seen his mark drop 9 lbs from 76 to 67, making him well-handicapped. His two runs this season have been promising. First, he finished 4th behind Isari at Musselburgh, needing the run after six months off. He then led boldly at Thirsk, only to be nabbed late by Mole Renan and Super Hit, pulling clear of the rest. Hamilton favours front runners, especially those securing the far rail. Callum Rodriguez takes the reins today, having ridden Swift Salian once before. Despite only one win in the 17 starts, he's hit the frame five times and thrives under ideal conditions. With a stiff mile and soft ground, he should have a strong chance to dictate from the stalls.

Ayr Poet's recent 2nd over course and distance gives encouragement for this contest. Jim Goldie is usually dangerous to write off at this local track. Sitting near the bottom of the weights with a 7lb claimer aiding the cause, Ayr Poet is a decent price to go one better this time around.
Very disappointing last time, but I have a feeling that Dingwall can look to bounce back after that pretty subpar effort last time.
Looking for a decent each way now, dropped a class and now going for the mile, which is what they think it wants. Blufferonthebus gets some going with a little ease in it. Looks a placer at least.

Bellasio is lightly raced but has shown bits and pieces of form. He may not be the easiest to keep right as he has been off the track more than on it. But judged on what he has achieved, he could be well suited by today's conditions and looks worth an each-way punt.

Trojan Soldier steps up to 1m4f after a strong second over 1m2f on handicap debut at Beverley, where he stayed on well late. His pedigree suggests further improvement over this longer trip. With an unchanged mark of 69, he looks well treated to build on that effort.

JOYFUL SOUND is an Ed Walker trained racer who makes the long journey up to Scotland. She races in the style of a filly who needs this stiffer test of stamina and on her handicap debut having likely saved some of her ability she appeals.
Another one from this stable who has been sent on this long journey to take part. Has run well over this trip in the last 2 outings and once again is not here to make the numbers up, you would think.

Back down in class in easier company and enlists Clifford Lee for top jockey/trainer combo. Sure to appreciate this trip length and will appreciate the forecast showers just before post time. The one to beat.

Kings Scholar is the 2nd of Ed Walker's 3 entered runners at this meeting today. The 2-time 12f winner tries 13f for the 1st time, and providing he handles the extra furlong, then he will be tough to beat with Clifford Lee in the saddle.

Letsbefrank is a 5-year-old gelding trained by Jim Goldie. He is 3/10 wins on turf and ridden by Paul Mulrennan. He doesn't come here in the best of form after three disappointing runs, but it took three runs last year to get into the groove, coming to hand from May 24, finishing 4-1-1-3-2-1. He runs today off 76, his last winning mark under Paul Mulrennan. He is a course winner and is ground and trip versatile. Also, Jim Goldie is 27/159 wins in 12f handicaps at Hamilton since 2012 and 27/118 wins if 14-1 or less. He is 1-2-5-1-1-1-4 with his last seven runners 14-1 or less in 12f handicaps at Hamilton. So, Jim Goldie clearly targets these races, and Letsbefrank has to enter calculations representing a yard who are 7/31 wins in recent weeks.

Race 6 at Hamilton today is a Handicap (Class 4) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 2,629 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 5-year-old gelding Sectarius from the Edward Bethell yard, and will be ridden by Callum Rodriguez. This son of Ribchester is lightly raced and comes off a 6-month rest. Having competed over 1400m to 1600m in his first 5 efforts, it was evident he was crying out for more ground. His first try was over 2400m, and he duly won. His follow-up efforts have been good, and he runs fresh today with not any superstars, which should see him in the firing line.

SUGAR ROAD may fare better with a potential pointer that he is sent to this track. The Andrew Balding yard do well { 19% } from a significant sample-size when sending runners long distances and Balding is 4/13 { 31% } at this venue. Some clues possibly to think this one is ready to run a big race today.

Savrola took a while to get going after joining Dianne Sayer, but since being stepped up in trip, he has shown improved form. It could be argued he nicked the race last time out in a slowly run race, but the 2nd and 3rd there both won on their next start, so the form looks okay. Although up in class today, there could be more to come.

Ran well enough on stable debut last time, his first run for 7 months. He was left poorly placed and met trouble in running, so is worth a decent bet here. Dropped a pound and sure to be fitter for that last run.

Forza Orta looks interesting here based on his old form and impressive course record. Two of his 4 wins have come here, and he was also runner-up on his last start here. His last win came at York in August '23, but having failed to place in 10 starts since, he is now 9 lbs lower. The recent form is not great, but he had a wind operation last month, and if that sees him anywhere near his old form, he looks a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.
Has three course and distance wins and looks on a good mark now to go well again back here. 2 lb above last winning mark, but talented 7 lb apprentice on board adds to the chance.
1 from 5 on turf and a chance if transferring AW form over. Good strike rate and looks a bit overpriced in the market for a yard knocking on the door recently.
Both turf wins have come at Beverley, and this looks like another winnable race. Was unlucky to finish 4th when here latest and can make amends today.

6-year-old gelding sired by Dark Angel is a course and distance winner. He likes to front run, and if he can get out in front, he may play 'catch me if you can' tactics. Down in the handicap to 72 today from as high as 78 after his last win (here) off 66. Should give a good account if breaking OK.
6yo gelding Finbars Lad should be a lot sharper here today on 2nd run after a 202 day break. Wasn't disgraced lto when 5th of 8 at Yarmouth and drops in class here. Should be in the mix.

Only the second time that Orbaan finds himself in such low-quality racing as this, and that itself should be taken as a bit of a pointer. Has been disappointing but was second prior to the last race. Good chance.

Is back down 1f in trip today after finishing 8th at Thirsk over 8f on his seasonal reappearance 25 days ago. Broke the maiden tag at Southwell over 8f but is yet to win on turf but had a couple of decent placed runs at Doncaster & Haydock over today's trip last season. Trainer J. Camacho has a 100% strike rate here at the course this season with 4 wins from 4 & with a +LSP £32.95 in processes & this son of Ribchester is her only runner on today's card.

Solid run back on turf off today's mark of 61 @ Catterick Lto and they are a dual C/D winner here with a 40 percent course profile. Good jockey back up and very shrewd trainer who is 19 percent with a Lsp of 37.50 last 14 days, best here with her 4yo plus last 5 seasons, making current 9/1 decent Ew value in the race.

Temper Trap tends to improve around July - August, and most of his 12 wins have been in this period year after year. It may yet be early days, but who knows, he may improve earlier this year and perhaps a value each way bet.

Princess Niyla was an unlucky third here four days ago, hampered late when closing strongly. She’s back off the same mark of 65 and has winning form over this course and distance. With conditions in her favour and consistent recent efforts, she looks ready to strike.

Veteran who hasn't won for some time but has taken a big drop down the weights as a result and took a good step forward from reappearance when 3rd off this mark here a fortnight ago. Looks ready to strike.
Lightly raced for a 4 year old, but that may play into this filly's advantage in what looks to be a fairly exposed field.

Mystical Maria is on an attractive mark at the moment, and she ran a very good comeback race last month at the track, coming third against a couple of subsequent winners. She will probably be better for the run, and the step up in distance should suit, given she has won over 9 furlongs at stiff Carlisle. Jockey Barry McHugh rode a winner for the owners four days ago, which counts as a positive.

Preference here goes to the Harriet Bethell trained, Bearwith. Previous C&D winner that makes his seasonal return after a lengthy spell on the sidelines. Despite that, he does hold a solid reappearance record and he looks fairly well treated on past form. Holds tendencies to be keen, so that could be a concern given the break. That said, he does stay this trip and he's weighted to be involved off his career best around this time last year. Only 3lb separate the field on RP ratings, so this double figure price holds strong appeal.
DANDY'S ANGEL wasn't a million miles behind Princess Niyla last time out so is given an each-way whirl in case she's able to match her once again.
This horse has raced well in slightly better company and lately in a race where the sectionals probably did not suit. But today, it may get an easier time.
Ruth Carss' Hostelry has been in great form of late and can go in again here. She is back up to 60 but has won off marks in the 60s in the past 3 years, so it is well within her ability.

Distinction returns to the scene of his victory in this race last year, having shown a solid third at Doncaster in March. His recent efforts have been in stronger company, and this drop back to Class 6 could see him more competitive. With a course-and-distance record and a mark of 59, he looks well placed to bounce back.

Dr Rio is a familiar face around this track, with 4 career wins here, and now finds himself 1 pound below his last winning mark. A 4-time winner at this course, he was unlucky last time as he did not get a clear run in the final furlong, yet still stayed on. The conditions look fine today with good to firm predicted, and he relishes this C&D.
6yo gelding Panama City was a good 2nd of 10 lto over 1m at Ripon. Is 7lbs below his AW mark and jockey takes of another 7lbs. Will be in the mix.
No comment made

Phoenix Fire is one of my tracked horses and has a bit of a patchy and frustrating profile, having not won since his debut in 2022 and ending last season poorly. However, he is very lightly raced for his age and now returns from a break, which could spark improvement. The opening market vibes may be telling here. EW shout.

In terms of the last race of Rogue Invader, the horses that have come out of that have raced to a better mark than these horses offer. Should be able to put this one away with top jockey Rossa Ryan on.

Saliko ran well on her stable debut after a 6-month layoff, finishing 2nd in a 3-runner maiden at Brighton over 7f. The small field might limit the form's depth, but the fact she went off 5/4 favourite suggests she was expected to go close and did little wrong in defeat.

Well held last time out when racing too keenly. Had gone close on first two starts before that though. 2nd at Newcastle over 7f and 2nd again at Ayr on turf debut. That was over 1m. Tried the longer trip of 1m1 last time out but, as stated, already raced too keenly and didn't see out that trip. Drop back down to 7f will suit here and hood also fitted.
The yard is in form, so I'm taking a bit of a chance on this unraced 5-year-old. There must have been problems training the mare, but the owner's patience could be rewarded today.

5yo irish gelding Fortunate Star was 3rd of 13 lto over 5f at Catterick. The winner of that race followed up with a 2nd place and the 3rd has won. Has won on todays ground conditions and off 5lbs higher last year, so should be in the mix.
Astapor is very well weighted compared to previous winning form over the minimum trip and finished a respectable 3rd at Wolverhampton on return to action in March.

IFONLYTHEYCUDTALK returns to last winning mark, which was over this distance and from this weight back in September. Given a look here in similar conditions and will have a pace to aim at and avoids a really high draw, so could be a player. Going shouldn't be a problem and looks a worthy each-way punt with the extra place to go for.

Showed signs of revival from a sliding handicap mark when only beaten by 1 length last time out at Wolverhampton. Races near the bottom of weights and has a 7lb claimer to aid the cause further. Looks overpriced at double-figure odds.

Desert Master last won on the AW in January off a 56. Although having no wins on turf yet, he did show improvement when returning from a short break and wind surgery to a fourth, when seeming to get the hang of things on the run in. I would expect more improvement today, now second up EW 4P.

U Turn is a 2-year-old colt trained by Tim Easterby, who is having an unusually good year-to-date with his 2-year-olds - 6/28 wins. U Turn is 6-7 in two starts and is dropped into a class 6 for the first time but has shown some decent form and may have been found a good opportunity today. Finished 6/8 on debut beaten only 3l behind Ice Cold Alex (RPR 73), Saucy Jane (RPR 64), Bravo Hotel (RPR 64), and Under The Radar (RPR 67), and they have since recorded RPRs of 82, 84, 80, and 79 respectively. Today's contest should be well within U Turn's grasp and is my short-priced banker of the day despite top weight.

Most of the runners here have finished closer to the rear of their rivals in their races. But there is tons of potential on pedigree, and the Dandy Man progeny, Dinamo, could improve to make the places.
Laser Focus has been out of form recently on the AW but returns to the turf, 10 lbs below his last winning mark. If he can recapture his best form, he would take some beating off his current rating.

Twoforthegutter comes into the race with arguably the best form. His second over a mile and three quarters at Carlisle last time looks fairly solid. The two in 3rd and 4th place were last time out winners, and Agathon, the winner, was beaten only a nose the next time. Twoforthegutter is versatile in regard to both trip and going and won off this mark last year. The gamble on Laser Focus is fascinating, but he looks like he will need a lot more than just a return to 12 furlongs to be competitive.
Bargain basement stuff in this race, with this horse showing prior course and distance form, as well as a pretty game reappearance for the season last time. Should place.
A well backed 5/4 favourite when beaten by a nose at Warwick earlier this month and can gain some compensation here off the same handicap mark.
Stinginhisstep made a big improvement on his handicap debut two weeks ago. He showed lots of immaturity but may improve and challenge for honors in this moderate lineup.

LA TRATTARIA could be anything and her opening mark can only realistically be a guess. She is a four year old filly in receipt of weight allowances and she could be well placed by her shrewd trainer. Interesting French sire could mean she has maturity beyond her years and she needs a market check.

Hurst Hill ran well here twice last year, both times keeping on 3rd over 2m1f (on good and on soft). Ran a couple of good races since at similar trips but failed to last over 3m others. Looks to have been learning and not asked a serious question when returning from break last time. Likely to be asked more of today returned here, and if finding best form, has a much better chance than 20/1 odds suggest.
Ran as well as ever last time behind a short-priced, classy Dan Skelton horse, which has won even easier since. This race is very weak and won't get many better opportunities.

All runs come from good ground, pointer winner and bumper runner-up. Jamie Snowden and Gavin Sheehan are in great form. Sharp Glance will go off as favourite, but Jack N Jones is a great match. Expect Gavin to go for all around this tight course.
Decent form and placed in a Bumper. Recent form hints at a stronger running today. Each-way bet offers a balance between risk and reward. One to watch. Improving.
Was a course and distance winner last time out and looks to be still very much ahead of the handicapper, so is likely to be able to win again here today.
Drops down markedly in class here, and this presents a good opportunity. Conditions will be fine, and Chadwick taking off 5 pounds helps. Should go close.
Caught the eye with how he finished over 20f last time. So the step back up in trip here is sure to suit, and he comes here from an unchanged mark.
Paddy De Pole has been running well without getting its head in front. It should run its race again here today, and with luck in running and jumping, could gain a well-deserved victory.
Started off over hurdles before switching to chases, picking up two wins from five at the start of the career. Could be between any of these but like a strong challenge here.

The model I run suggests an upset by Borderline. This result has been driven by Borderline having a very similar RPR to the rest of the field, but has a significantly lower official ranking. This subsequently means Borderline goes out carrying a lot less weight than the rest of the field. There is over a stone difference to every other runner and nearly 2 (!) to the top weight. Borderline is running for the first time post wind operation and might just cause an upset if getting off to a good start. The model has indicated a 'very low' stake reading which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of to 4.

The model I run suggests Cap Du Mathan should win this race. Cap Du Mathan lines up here with the second highest RPR of this 6-runner field. It also has the second highest official ranking but comes here in decent form and should be able to handle the small extra weight. Olive Nichols picks up the reins and relieves 3 lbs off the extra weight, which helps around this 2m 4f trip. The model has indicated a 'very low' staking indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of to 4. This is largely due to the very small gap in win probability percentage back to the horse who came second in the race simulation, Yccs Portecervo.

Cap Du Mathan is clearly a talented opponent but is quite out of his range here, clearly preferring 2m3 at the most. On Springs dominated the PTPs this year but might struggle a bit in this area. On the other hand I've been following YCCS PORTOCERVO recently and although the last few runs have been a bit off the boil, he finds himself in comfortable territory here. Distance and going sure to suit, as it did in this competition last year when running away easily with it. He was never going to get anywhere at Aintree, and last time out was a trip too far, so I'm not overly concerned. Only 4lbs above last year's win so wiggle room. Here's hoping for a good performance.

The model I run suggests Daring Plan can win this one. Daring Plan lines up with the highest RPR of this 7-runner field. Does go out carrying the second highest amount of weight for the privilege. Comes here in decent form and is running only the second race post successful wind operation. The model has indicated a 'very low' staking indicator for the race, predominantly due to the very small margin back to second place in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Radharc Na Slaine ran well when 2nd over course and distance last July and is now down to his lowest ever mark of 70 and should at least get placed again to make the trip from Pembrokeshire to Devon worthwhile.
In a moderate lineup, the Yeats progeny Sevenofus is fancied to build on recent improvement shown in her penultimate start when finishing second over 4400m.

Won first time up last season and was generally progressive. Makes seasonal reappearance off the same mark as he ended last year on, which is 7lb higher than winning 2 runs back by over 7l. So, he has a decent chance on the numbers, especially with the runner-up to him winning next time and going on to subsequently win several more races.

Kick Up a Storm has some decent form over hurdles and could be anything going over fences for the first time. But I think the value is with Hold Your Fort. He has 4 wins and a second from 6 goes at the track, with the unplaced effort coming on soft ground that wouldn't have suited. He has won off 2lb higher than his current mark in the past and was a good second here last time out.

Last 2 events at today's distance, finished 2nd & 3rd on today's mark, not far away from the winners. With today's rival Deise Aba some 11 lengths behind in 6th place, when finishing a credible 2nd. The winner that day had won class 2 events and entered class 1 events since the win.
They are stepping this one back up in trip with the same jockey on board. Worth a small EW saver bet.
Top jockey on board, Oisin Murphy. Top yard too. Yard won this race in 2021 and 2023. Got a feeling about this one.

Palmitate ran well in Class 4 over five furlongs on debut, pulling hard but finishing well into third, well clear of the remainder. With that experience, dropping to Class 5 and stepping up to six furlongs, should be competitive here.
With the first two in the betting being at short-looking odds, it may pay to take a chance with this newcomer. The stable is doing well with its 2-year-olds, and the odds are more attractive.

Binhareer returns from a break and makes his first start since being gelded, now switching to handicap company. He won well at Redcar over 7f and starts life in handicaps off a mark of 81. With clear scope to progress and conditions in his favour, he looks a strong contender today.

Critical Acclaim lines up today after finishing second in both career starts over 7 furlongs on the all-weather, including a close effort at Wolverhampton. He remains unexposed and appears well suited to the surface and distance.

Left Charlie Johnston last year after 4 starts winning once and runner-up in another. Was gelded after joining Jamie Osbourne and there was a 301 day break before seeing him start off for his new yard at Lingfield (turf) earlier this month with a decent 4th of 10. Without watching that race the form means very little, but everything that could have gone wrong did and under the circumstances he did very well to manage that 4th place. If breaking from the stalls better here he could well outrun his odds.

Has a decent draw in stall 1 here. Spirit Lead Me is a course winner, so clearly capable on this track. However, recent form is below par, finishing 6 of 7 in a handicap at this course over 8f around 2 months ago. Has not shown strong form lately and looks out of sorts, but I'm giving him another chance here to bounce back.

Earlier in her career, Searchingtheblues secured a victory on 4 July 2024 at Kempton over 7 furlongs, winning a Class 5 novice stakes at odds of 50/1 . She followed up with another win on 29 July 2024 at Wolverhampton over the same distance . Her pedigree, being by Due Diligence out of the mare Blue Lyric (by Refuse To Bend), suggests a strong aptitude for sprint distances. 
In tomorrow's race at Kempton, she will compete over 7 furlongs in a Class 4 all-weather race. With her previous success over this course and distance, and the booking of jockey Oisin Murphy, Searchingtheblues appears poised to make a significant impact in this competitive field.
Big chance here. Race not run to suit on Hat Trick bid last time. Seems sure to get the strong pace he needs in this race, so is well worth backing here.
With money coming for several of these, this could drift to an each-way price. Has had excuses in all three of his runs this year, and with luck in running, will go close.

At double figure price with an extra place on offer I'll take a shot at Lucy Wadham's 7yo Estidhkaar gelding, who won over C&D on his penultimate start in March off a mark of 87 (he's on 89 here). He was beaten by a nose on that same mark earlier in March over C&D so I think he's in with a shout here.

Taking a bit of a punt here with Kotari. He finished 9th of 11 in a handicap at Epsom over 12f about 5 weeks ago. But from what I saw, he wasn't fully tested or pushed hard at all, which could mean the run was more of a fitness spin and a test to put backers off him (a tactic that some jockeys do use to reduce the form and mark sneakily). Today's run will be telling if he finishes anywhere near the post.

Very nicely bred horse and related to winners. Clearly not suited by heavy ground on last two starts as a 3yo last season, but prior run on soft @ Newmarket a more than decent one @ this level. Has had wind surgery and been given plenty of time to recover, retains a decent mark of 78 on 4yo return, good jockey up and very shrewd trainer who has recently hit form, is only 9 percent with his 4yo plus here last 5 seasons but with a very impressive Lsp of 85.58, making current 28/1 solid Ew value in the race.
Trojan Storm won on Tapeta after a break last time out. Although not so good on Poly here last year, he could be worth another shot after another short break. EW 4P.

Not a bad effort last time after a layoff over a distance that was likely to have been too short. That will have sharpened this horse up, and the addition of a more suitable distance and a jockey claiming 7lbs off his back makes this horse a tantalizing each-way prospect at huge odds. Still has scope being lightly raced so far.

If anyone reads this, I swear if this is beaten even with a penalty, I am never having a bet at Kempton All Weather again. If I drop dead now, I would not have done. The long straight at Kempton makes ordinary horses look like Pegasus, and the selection looked just such a horse last time. It has a penalty today, and there are dangers lurking in the wings. If it wins, it might be decent. If it loses, bread and jam for tea.

Fort Campbell is a lightly raced 3-year-old colt with just 2 starts. He improved markedly from debut to finish 3rd of 11 in a Chelmsford novice over 7f in October, but has been off since, so this will be his seasonal reappearance. He is now open to significant improvement, now returning as a 3-year-old. That Chelmsford effort showed plenty of promise, staying on well. Likely to be fitter and more mature now, and the form of that race has more potential depth, and he can run well here.
Top jockey Jim Crowley is booked for this race. 9-3 weights are too low, so he is up for a good chance. Each way claims at least.

Khafiz returns after a year off, having finished 14th of 20 on debut at Newbury over 6f. He now steps up to 7f and wears a hood for the first time, suggesting potential improvement. His pedigree indicates he should handle the surface, and the stable has a strong record with similar types.

Beautifully bred and cost 750k as a yearling. Was green as grass on debut last time and finished well once the penny dropped. Steps up to 7f here, which will suit and will come on for that initial experience.

Nutmeg drops back to 7f after weakening late over a mile at Newbury, suggesting this shorter trip suits better. He previously finished second over 7f on the all-weather, showing strong early speed. With first-time cheekpieces applied and a return to a more suitable distance, he looks poised to build on that earlier promise.

Race 4 at Kempton today is a Novices (Class 4) for 3-year-olds and upwards over 1,408 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 3-year-old gelding Both Of Us from the George Boughey yard. He will be ridden by Patrick Cosgrave. This son of Magna Grecia is on debut today and is a half-brother to the highly rated Spangled Mac from the same yard. In a race where anyone could win, he could easily be one, especially on breeding.

Kameko filly. She is a half-sister to the 1m-11f winner Ezaj and the 9f winner She Is Invincible. Her Dam, who raced twice, is half-sister to the talented Hazel Lavery, a winner up to 1 and half mile. The pedigree is encouraging, but with the odds currently at 20/1, I would recommend an each-way bet.

Won on 5th attempt recently at Wolverhampton by a length on step up to one mile four furlongs. This comes on the back of two 2nds including one here at Kempton. Could be more progress here, and goes off at bottom weight from a decent low draw.
Ran well enough on reappearance run last time, doing all her best work in the latter stages. Of interest here, stepped up in trip and dropping a pound.
Nowhere ran a decent 4th of 12 over this C&D about 7 weeks ago at decent odds. The fact it was a solid placing, and if conditions remain similar today, Nowhere could be somewhere in the fiinish.

Won with plenty in hand at Wolverhampton three starts ago and ran a good third over course and distance next time. Returned to all-weather here and dropped a pound. Can go well at a big price. Each-way Nap at 10/1.
Kinetic won the last two, and the 4 lbs rise and stepping up to C4 might not be enough to stop a hat-trick while keeping Mason in the saddle and his 7 lbs claim.

Has shown promise in all 5 of her last starts and boasts a dominant C&D win from off the pace last time out here in December. If picking up where she left off, absolutely no reason she shouldn't be up there in the final yards.

The jockey and trainer combination can be fruitful to follow. This selection showed enough promise on a recent course outing where the step up in trip elicited improvement on previous showings. There is plenty of scope for further progress.

Gooloogong returns to the same course and distance after a narrow victory over Capone, showing a strong finish to lead in the final 100 yards. Raised just 2lbs, he remains competitively weighted and has previously outperformed several of today’s rivals.
Orchestra made all here last month and could be worth another shot on the return with a handy 5 lbs claimer in the saddle to help out while up just 3 lbs.

Capone runs in the 20:52 at Kempton tomorrow and looks like a strong each-way contender. He was last seen just a couple of weeks ago on 15th May at this very track and distance, finishing 2nd of 8 in a competitive Class 5 handicap. That run showed he's in good heart and handles the surface well. He stayed on nicely that day, suggesting he’s still got plenty to offer at this trip.
What makes him even more appealing this time is the booking of Oisin Murphy, a notable upgrade in the saddle that signals clear intent. He’s well treated on past form and looks to have been placed cleverly by the yard. With recent form in the book, a proven liking for the course and trip, and one of the best jockeys riding, Capone looks a solid bet to go one better this time.
Kissininthebackrow last won here in October when running off a 60 in C6. I think the return here after two duff turf runs could see a revival off a 61 with Hollie Doyle EW.

Class 5, 2 mile handicap, last race on the card at Kempton. Lusaka is yet to win on the AW (only two previous attempts) but boasts a career record of 5 wins from 30 races. Former winner at Class 2 level from OR72 and runs off a mark of 71 here. Out of form with very poor run at Chester last time. That was first race back for six months. Longshot but should have more chance than a 66-1 shot.

Just about an each-way price having destroyed a field off 48 on penultimate start. Unable to follow up under the penalty last time and is now 11lb higher than the win. On the numbers, shouldn't be far away with 5lb claimer on top.

Stella Hogan, a five-year-old chestnut mare trained by Michael Appleby and owned by The Horse Watchers 11, is scheduled to compete in the 17:18 Unibet More Extra Place Races Apprentice Handicap at Kempton on Wednesday, 28 May 2025. In her most recent outing on 27 March 2025 at Chelmsford City, she finished sixth in a Class 6 handicap over 7 furlongs, beaten by 6¾ lengths .
Earlier in the season, Stella Hogan secured a victory on 8 March 2025 at Chelmsford City, winning a Class 6 handicap over 7 furlongs . She has demonstrated consistency with a record of 3 wins, 6 second-place finishes, and 3 third-place finishes from 25 starts .
In tomorrow's race at Kempton, she will compete over 1 mile in a Class 5 all-weather race. With her recent form and experience over similar distances, Stella Hogan appears poised to make a significant impact in this competitive field. Back up to 1 mile should suit for e/w value here.

LAW SUPREME takes his chance with the yard among the recent winners and is no doubt a well treated racer against his best form. He appeared a shade unlucky when last seen at thjs track and over this distnace , so the feeling is he should be ready to get involved tonight.

Mbappe was well supported at 4/1 last time out but ran no race at all, finishing last of 13 over 7f at this course. That effort was out of character considering he is a previous course winner. The market support on the last run suggests connections expected better, so it’s possible something was amiss that day. Now potentially better treated if bouncing back and giving him another chance here.

Only 1-20 but had been running well off higher marks during the winter before some poor turf efforts so far this spring. Returns to the all-weather on a very interesting mark now, so very much of interest on that basis.

The Dominic Ffrench Davis-trained Cherry Hill admittedly has been disappointing this season in her two starts so far at Lingfield and at Brighton. However, she has dropped to a handy mark, and although she races 2 lbs out of the handicap, jockey Isobelle Chalmers takes off 5 lbs to leave Cherry Hill well in and carrying a bottom weight of just 7-13 (net). Her sole win came here off a mark of 58, and she has 2 places from 6 starts at Kempton. Speculative e/w punt at good odds.

The handicapper has dropped him 1 lb for the last run. Running off just a 2 lbs higher mark than his last win. He goes well at this venue. Form figures 112423233 at this venue, which improve to 112223 when running over this CD. He's won off marks of 100 and 107, and also placed off marks of 120, 109, and 105 here. So very much on a nice enough mark. Running off just 102 today. He ran okay last time out, finishing a clear 2nd behind easy winner Lively Citizen. He was giving 5 lbs in weight to the winner. Sean Bowen takes over this time. I think he can go one better today.
Richie McLernon in chases at Cartmel - 23% SR - +£45.03 LSP to a £1 stake. First run for Haslam yard - 23% SR in chases at the track, +£25.53 to £1 stake LSP.

The model I run indicates Sword Of Fate can cause an upset here in this larger 13-runner field. Sword Of Fate has the highest RPR of all the runners here by quite an amount. Official ranking looks materially lower and subsequently goes out carrying less weight than the potential suggests he can achieve. Plenty of course and distance winners here and Sword Of Fate is one of them. Last ran 13 days ago, so race fitness should be good and can make an impression here if ready. The market has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of to 4.

Militaire has placed in all four chase starts, including a solid second at Uttoxeter over 3 miles. He now drops back in trip and wears first-time cheekpieces, which could sharpen his focus. Although 5lb out of the handicap, his consistency and adaptability to softer ground suggest he can remain competitive in this small field.
Richie McLernon in Chases at Cartmel - 23% SR - +£45.03 LSP to a £1 Stake. Winner on Saturday. Well treated under a penalty.
Won maiden hurdle over course and distance at last year's meeting. This step back up to this trip will suit, having been outpaced over shorter last time before running on.

The model I run suggests Rioja Alta can win this one. Rioja Alta lines up with the joint highest RPR of this 10-runner field. Rioja Alta does have the second lowest official ranking here, so the weight being carried is a lot lower than the current market leaders. There is a 1 stone 5 lbs difference to the current market leader, which is significant over this 2m 6f trip. Rioja Alta comes here after a short break, having last run 74 days ago, but that was a win. Coming here in similar form should see Rioja Alta over the line first. The model has indicated a 'very low' stake reading, which translates to a 0.5 pt bet on a scale of to 4.

This Class 4 handicap hurdle over 2m 6f can go the way of the in-form Jamie Snowden-trained Golden Maverick. The 5-year-old gelding has been given a 79-day break after his uncharacteristic fall at the last in an unsuitably short trip of 16 1/2f Class 3 handicap hurdle. The former 5-time winner on the flat has won 3 and placed in 3 out of his 10 hurdle races since being bought out of the Ian Williams yard to go juvenile hurdling. He should relish this ground, and the step up in trip might bring about a bit more improvement. If he stays, then he should have a great chance this evening.

The model I run suggests The Jeweller's Pet can win this one. The Jeweller's Pet lines up here with the joint highest RPR of this 10-runner field but has the second lowest official ranking. This subsequently means The Jeweller's Pet goes out carrying less weight than the majority of runners here. Ala Doyle on board relieves a further 5 lbs, which helps over this 2m 6f trip. The model has indicated a 'very low' stake reading, which is largely driven by the small win probability % gap back to second place in the race simulation.

Achnamara is a dual purpose gelding who's been in good form over hurdles this year but disappointed on his return to the flat. 2 wins from last 3 hurdle runs shows he's in decent form over timber and the latest hurdle win came in a competitive handicap at Catterick, where he saw the trip out well. The unseat at Kelso was just unfortunate, so you can forgive that error. Still fairly treated on some of his better jumps form and handles good to soft ground. EW or win chance here.
Won a similar hunter chase last time after 16 months off. His wins previously have come after breaks. This 3-month break is a relatively quick turnaround, but hopefully, he can follow up here.

The model I run suggests Great Notions can win this one. This result has been driven by Great Notions having a relatively high RPR compared to some of the other runners, and a reasonable weight to carry. All horses go out carrying within 4 lbs of each other in terms of initial weight around this 3m 1f track. Great Notions comes here in exceptional form with figures of 3132-1 and looks to add another win to his name here as he progresses. Youngest of the field by quite a bit, so looks to progress again with Mr. Dawson picking up the reins. The model has issued a 'low' reading indicator which translates to a 0.75pt stake on a scale of 0-4.
Point winner last time and well treated on novice form. Prolific in form under the right conditions and a consistent runner. Each way bet at this price is too good to turn down, big threat.

Usually gives his all here and his latest third over C&D off 13lb higher reads extremely well. A pipe-opener without the usual cheekpieces at Perth last month should have blown away the cobwebs and this race looks extremely winnable.

The model I run suggests Belle of Annandale can cause an upset here. Belle of Annandale lines up with by far the highest RPR of this 10-runner field. Looks well treated in the official ranking and subsequently goes out carrying a lower weight than the market front runners. Belle of Annandale typically settles in mid-division, which might suit the tight course here at Cartmel. This race today also represents a drop in class. The model has issued a 'very low' staking indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of to 4. This is a result of the small gap back to second place in terms of win probability % in the race simulation.

Mr Sundancer is a modest hurdler who finally got his head in front at Downpatrick last summer and now looks to be slowly finding form again. Winner over hurdles last year with the hood back on now, and the stable switch to a new yard (left Shark Hanlon) and latest run at Sedgefield was a step back in the right direction, finishing 4th after a break. Can go well if building on that comeback effort, especially now race-fit again.

The model I run suggests Terrorise can win this one. Terrorise lines up here with a fairly middle-ranking RPR but looks well treated on the weights. Goes out carrying the second lowest amount of weight here around this 2m 1f race. Placed well in third only 19 days ago, so comes here in good form. The model has issued a 'very low' staking indicator largely due to the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of to 4.

Love True is a modest hurdler so far with eight winless attempts over timber, but there's a little more to note now with this change of scenery. A flat winner in France, so has a baseline of ability. Stable switch to Rebecca Menzies, who often does well with new recruits. Has shown bits of form in the past that could see her sneak into a place, especially in this weaker contest.

BITTALEMON may have needed her comeback run and this yard target their runners at this specific spring meeting. This Dubawi-sired four year old has potential to improve significantly on the back of that effort and the market can reveal more.
This should be a race that is contended between the top two in the market. I prefer the chances of Beacon Edge, who is a multiple winner on today's going and will be fresh from a layoff.

The model I run suggests Redwood Queen should win this one. This result has been driven by Redwood Queen having the highest RPR of the 7-runner field. Has an official rating that is reasonably kind here too and carries over a stone less than the current market leader, Beacon Edge. Redwood Queen is a previous distance winner and last ran 17 days ago, so race fitness should not be a concern. The model issued a 'very low' staking indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of to 4.

Fell on chase debut last time and quickly reverts to hurdles, over which he was placed a couple of times last autumn. No world-beater, but on these terms, he might just be able to split the market leaders.
Faded quite badly when favourite for a handicap at Tipperary last time out but has good course form and Darragh O'Keeffe to keep his mind on the job here and should win.

This is the trainer's only entry he's got out today, and they have got a 7 lbs claiming jockey booking/change. A good value each-way bet for 4 places is available. Also, dropping it back down in trip.

SIDIRIYA is clearly well handicapped under this code as a former Dermot Weld trained 84 rated flat racer. She was effective when fresh previously and has been given time by ace dual-purpose trainer Philip Rothwell. Second look at a handicap hurdle race here and with a talented 5lb claiming conditional jockey aboard she appeals.

You’ll need to look past the glaring 0000-0 formline staring back at you from tomorrow’s Racing Post or The Irish Field to even consider backing Paul Flynn’s 5-year-old gelding PENSION PLAN. And yes, on that basis, 50/1 looks about right. But this son of YEATS actually showed a flicker of promise on handicap debut at Sligo (20f, Good). He led from flag fall and only gave way two out - hardly the stuff of total dismissal.
Now he drops 3 furlongs in trip and 3lbs in the weights, switching to a sharp, flat, left-handed track which, on paper at least, looks more in his favour. A quick glance into his bloodlines even suggests a preference for going left-handed, adding a touch more interest.
Jockey Gavin Brouder keeps the ride and takes a valuable 3lbs off. He’s shown a solid return at Wexford over the past five years with a 30% place strike rate. Trainer Paul Flynn echoes that with a 33% place record at the track and a notable 25% strike rate with his second-time-out handicappers.
So if you’re willing to look beyond the surface gloom, there’s just enough to justify an each-way nibble at that whopping 50/1.

Son of Anarchy has been struggling to finish his races strongly, but has been running in much better company than this. He has got a fantastic pedigree for National Hunt racing and it will be disappointing if he can't win this.
Has had chances in his last two races but has made significant jumping errors at crucial stages of both those races. Worth one last chance in the hope he can put his jumping together.

Avalo is a lightly raced maiden under National Hunt rules. The recent run was 8th of 17 in a novice hurdle at Down Royal over 17f. Did not look in top form recently, possibly still needing a bit more experience. However, a chance is taken for an EW play here, so we will see.

The model I run suggests an upset here by Hurricane Bailey. Hurricane Bailey lines up here with a relatively middle order RPR compared to the other 9 runners, but looks well treated in weights and goes out carrying 7-14 lbs less than the rest of the field. The model has indicated a 'moderate' reading for staking, which translates to a 1 pt bet on a scale of to 4.
A class above these rivals though can throw in a below par performance so not one to get heavily involved with but if anywhere near his best he wins.
Won at today's distance and conditions with ease. Likely to see another bold run here. Had a prep run recently, seems to come on, based on past history of runs.

The model I run suggests So Des Flos can win this one. So Des Flos lines up here with the second lowest RPR of the 4 runners here but also carries the joint lowest weight. This looks like a very open race. The model has indicated a 'very low' stake indicator for that reason, driven predominantly by the very small gap between all 4 runners in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of to 4.

The model I run suggests Sunchart should win this race. Sunchart lines up here with a fairly middle-ranking order but carries slightly less weight than the majority of the runners over this 2m 1f trip. Mr. Ryan on board relieves a further 7 lbs, which can be noticeable over this distance and takes Sunchart down to the second lowest weight being carried on the racecard. Comes here after a long break, so reliant on Sunchart running well fresh, but showed exceptional form before the long break with form figures of 3/212-. Prior course and distance winner, so knows how to get it done here. The model has indicated a 'very low' staking indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of to 4. This is largely driven by the small winning probability % margin back to the horse placed in second in the race simulation, Farfromnowhere.
Only out of the frame once in five starts over hurdles and should be there or thereabouts again with any rain that falls decidely in his favour.

It may be hard to peg back the favorite, but the E.J. O'Grady gelding is no mug and can muddy the waters if back on song despite being beaten favorite last time. Two pounds difference from last race and has won at this distance.

Duke Of Leggagh had some excellent form on the flat as a 3-year-old, including being beaten just 1.75 lengths by subsequent Group 1 winner Paddington at Naas in March 2023. He switched to hurdles last winter and won twice at Naas in February and March. Both of those wins were on soft ground. He returned to the flat with an excellent win at Roscommon two weeks ago, and with rain forecast, he looks a good EW bet here.

This selection's best effort to date was a 7th place finish over the distance of 16 furlongs in a class 2. Racing around 17 furlongs in today's contest, hopeful the ground will suit. Darragh O'Keeffe is in the saddle. Has each-way appeal.

The model I run suggests Ballycommon Chapel should win this one. Ballycommon Chapel lines up here with the highest RPR of this larger 14-runner field. Ballycommon Chapel is well treated off this official ranking, leaving him carrying the third lowest weight of this racecard. Conor Owens on board relieves a further 7 lbs, which can be telling over this distance of 2m 1f. That's a total weight differential of over 2 stone to the top weight and market rival Pampar Lady. Ballycommon Chapel also ran 14 days ago, so race fitness should not be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' staking indicator, largely due to 4.5 (7/2) being considered expensive for the win probability % here in this larger 14-runner field. This 'very low' reading translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of to 4.
Much improved last season, finishing a runner-up on 3 occasions. Now making seasonal return on a competitive mark in a weak race.
Responded well to this jockey at Down Royal last time out. Any improvement on that effort may well prove good enough this evening.

POLLY POPPINS wears the hood and is a Pour Moi-sired mare who has been fancied and punted through her qualifying campaign. Top conditional jockey Tiernan P R rode her when last seen , so will know what to expect and presumably throught capable she could be out to land some bets.
Best form is as a hurdler, with 2 of 4 career wins coming at this venue. Has been running well enough considering advancing years. Not without each way hope.

The model I run suggests Kildinan Prince can win this one. Kildinan Prince lines up here with the highest RPR of this 14-runner field, and the majority of horses go out carrying the same amount of initial weight. Lots of claiming jockeys in this national hunt flat, and Mr. Ryan, who picks up the reins, is one of them. This isn't necessarily an advantage given so many others are claiming, but it's worth noting Kildinan Prince isn't at a disadvantage for others claiming. Comes here after a decent second 14 days ago and looks to progress and go one better today. The model has issued a 'moderate' stake indicator for this one, meaning a 1pt bet on a scale of to 4.
Has put up 3 decent NHF race runs to date and very good amateur has been booked here, making current 8.50 the Ew play in the race.

Hawks Rock is a tentative selection as he hasn't run under rules yet, but he has a nice pedigree, being by Jukebox Jury and out of a decent Martaline mare. The trainer doesn't have many bumper winners but he did introduce the useful Ma Shantou to run a very good 3rd at Fairyhouse before being sold to England to run for Emma Lavelle.
Kevlar makes its debut for the Tony Martin yard in the last here at Wexford. It has placed in a N/H flat race and could run a big race for its new yard here tonight.

LAKEWOOD ROSE is a later-starting seven year old mare who was ridden by this jockey/trainer to win a PTP race in March. This more extreme distance in the Bumper sphere should suit having shown up well latest and a relatively quick turnaround reads well. Each-way appeal.

Butchers Bill's recent form was a good 6th of 17 in a competitive handicap hurdle over a marathon 23f distance at Naas. That run was solid, and he handled the strong test of stamina well. Runs for a top stable (Gordon Elliott) and with a break of nearly 2 months since the last run could mean he's fresh and ready to perform. Looks a solid contender with stamina proven over a long trip. His consistent efforts and yard credentials make him in with a shout here.

Decent point-to-point type who should excel when over bigger obstacles. But for now, Kyle Valley has done little over hurdles until beaten a head 3m latest wearing cheekpieces for just the second time. Winner has since gone close off 6lb higher and bumped form, and a claimer is put up for tonight.

ASHLIA DANCER is a player on this her handicap debut holding another entry in a relatively decent looking novice hurdle. She starts out as top-rated top weight potentially well treated and her claiming conditional jockey offers excellent value for the 7lb he is allowed.

NATIVE SONG seems likely to be suited by this step back up to three miles and her recent return run gives cause for optimism. She may have needed that latest effort , but does now at least have track form and the suspicion is she has scope from her current lowly mark.
Interesting runner here who does possess decent enough quality. I like the fact of the recent run to blow away any rust and could be set for a good run here.

By far her best run to date was when racing over 2m 7f last summer so this 3m shouldn't hold any terrors. Much lesser efforts over shorter trips since but looks fairly treated on this handicap debut and can get involved in the finish.

This is the trainer's only entry he's got out today, and they have got a good jockey booking/change as they are adding the first-time cheekpieces to the tongue tie on its handicap debut. Also, stepping up in trip, worth a small each-way saver bet for the 4 places available.

Looks like a fair bit of support for this one who has uninspiring figures, having been pulled up the last twice. But 3 runs back he caught the eye, just around a year ago when 3rd. Comes here 4lb lower trying new headgear. Been backed as if a good run is expected.

Still a maiden after 23 NH outings. She placed 13th of 17 in a handicap hurdle at Naas 55 days ago. Cheekpieces are back in play, she's down to a career-low rating and the conditions will be beneficial. With 4 places up for grabs, an each-way bet at 33/1 looks a fair opportunity.

Forty Kay is a 5-year-old daughter of No Risk at All ex Calakanga, who traces back to two great broodmares, namely Sweet Mimosa by Le Levanstell and Feemoss by Ballymoss. She makes her racecourse debut here in this mares-only bumper, where she'll be ridden by Mr. P.W. Mullins for his father W.P. Mullins, in the colors of the Blueblood Racing Club. Runners here with form may not be too strong, and it may be open to a newcomer to come to the fore on this occasion. I make my selection my Nap of the day.
